Critic: Affine registration of the frames is performed against frame0_ instead of maintaining a difference from the prior time frame.The tracking logic could be more robust if registration occurs between each pair of frames which would allow for pairwise union maps_ but without the increasing distortion from frame0 introducing additional error.Evaluating the difference in performance between those two approaches to justify the selection the algorithm made would support the paper.With the authors highlighting the longitudinal nature of the S1 type data_ the longer the timeframe the data spans the more mis-alignment and variance which can accumulate.Additionally_ the manuscript does not characterize the level of inter-frame distortion the registration step can handle before tracking results degrade.Characterization of the frame0 alignment accuracy delta is required for why t->0 is used instead of t-> t-1.
Answer: We appreciate the reviewer’s insightful comments regarding our choice of registration strategy in the framework. The decision to perform affine registration against frame 0 (t→0) in the S1 scenario is intentional and specifically tailored to the unique characteristics of the data and our tracking objectives. In the S1 scenario_ where there is low relative object motion but high global deformation_ registering all frames to the first frame (t→0) allows us to verify when an object exits and re-enters the region of interest. This global alignment is crucial for closing gaps in visibility for individual objects that temporarily leave the field of view. By assuming that the object's last visible position moved out of frame and then returned_ we can correct for tracking errors caused by temporary occlusions or exits from the visible region. This approach is particularly effective in scenarios such as protein accumulations_ where there is no relative motion between objects. Additionally_ global registration to t=0 allows us to correct for cumulative misalignment and variance over longer timeframes_ which is critical for longitudinal data_ thereby minimizing the risk of compounding errors that could arise from sequential pairwise registration (t→t-1).In scenarios with high relative object motion (S2)_ we switch to registering frames to the previous frame (t→t-1). This approach minimizes motion between consecutive frames_ ensuring that the union map accurately connects tracks without conflating distinct objects.

Answer: We appreciate the reviewer’s thoughtful feedback and the opportunity to clarify the unique contributions of our algorithm_ as the ability to work with multiple types of images is indeed a shared trait among tracking-by-detection (TBD) algorithms due to their reliance on pre-segmented objects. However_ the primary novelty and strength of MOLT lie in its graph-based conflict resolution and its capability to assign provenance to complex morphological events_ such as multiple cells splitting from a single cell. To better highlight these specific advantages_ we have revised the manuscript to include quantitative comparisons demonstrating how MOLT performs robustly across both S1 (low relative motion_ high global deformation) and S2 (high relative motion_ splitting_ and deformation) scenarios_ whereas other algorithms (e.g._ reference 21) may excel in S1 but struggle in S2. Additionally_ we emphasize MOLT’s unique benefits_ such as its ability to accurately track and assign lineage provenance in complex scenarios like cell division and splitting events_ which we quantitatively demonstrate through metrics capturing lineage accuracy and morphological event detection. We believe these revisions provide a clearer argument for the benefits of MOLT and substantiate our claims with quantitative results_ and we thank the reviewer for encouraging us to better articulate the strengths of our approach.
